phases: Technical foundation of the dark theme

cards.title: Inventory the screens, styles and routes of the app touched by dark mode
cards.body: Scope: frame the work before any code is written, for the Acme Notes web app. Steps: 1) list the 5 screens (note list, editor, search, settings, sharing dialog), their style sheets and the components they share; 2) note every place where a colour is hard-coded, with its file and line; 3) route each piece of work to the bot whose description fits it; 4) set the dependencies so that a review always follows the card it reviews. Out of scope: writing code, writing the content, judging the design. Acceptance criteria: every piece of work has an owner, a dependency and a way to be checked, and nothing is left implicit. Proof: the plan as one document, with the list of the cards and their dependencies.

cards.title: Add the dark colour tokens to tokens.css
cards.body: Scope: web/styles/tokens.css, from the inventory of the card cad1. Steps: 1) declare one custom property per colour role and its dark value under [data-theme=dark]; 2) replace the hard-coded colours of the inventory by the variables, without changing the light rendering; 3) check the result at 380 px and 1440 px, with the keyboard and with a pointer; 4) leave no error or warning in the console of the browser; 5) respect the reduced-motion preference for anything that moves; 6) run the build and the tests before handing over. Out of scope: the API, the content, a redesign of the screens that are not named. Acceptance criteria: no regression of the existing screens, keyboard use works end to end and the console stays empty. Proof: the diff, the output of the tests and before and after screenshots.

cards.title: Build the theme toggle and the no-flash script
cards.body: Scope: a toggle component in plain JavaScript and the inline script that sets the theme before the first paint. Steps: 1) read the stored choice, then prefers-color-scheme, and set data-theme on the root element; 2) store the choice on click and expose the state to assistive technology; 3) leave no error or warning in the console of the browser; 4) respect the reduced-motion preference for anything that moves; 5) run the build and the tests before handing over; 6) keep the existing components and class names where they already do the job. Out of scope: the server code, the copy of the interface, any new dependency. Acceptance criteria: the build passes, the rendering matches the reference on every screen named and nothing shifts while the page loads. Proof: the output of the build and screenshots of each state at both widths.

cards.title: Review the dark tokens and the contrast ratios
cards.body: Scope: the diff of the card thcss. Steps: 1) compare each token with the inventory and look for a colour left outside the variables; 2) measure the contrast of the text and background pairs yourself instead of trusting the report; 3) number each finding and say how to reproduce it; 4) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked; 5) measure it yourself instead of trusting the report of the card; 6) run the build and the tests again and quote their real output; 7) look for a regression next to the change, not only in it. Out of scope: fixing what you find yourself. Acceptance criteria: every criterion of the card reviewed is checked one by one and the verdict follows from the findings. Proof: the numbered findings and the commands that were run.

cards.title: Review the toggle and the no-flash script
cards.body: Scope: the diff of the card thjs. Steps: 1) read the script for the three cases stored choice, system preference and nothing at all; 2) load a page with a cold cache in both themes and watch the first paint; 3) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked; 4) measure it yourself instead of trusting the report of the card; 5) run the build and the tests again and quote their real output; 6) look for a regression next to the change, not only in it. Out of scope: rewriting the deliverable, widening the scope of the card reviewed. Acceptance criteria: a global verdict with numbered findings, each one reproducible, and nothing validated that was not checked. Proof: the review report with the real output of the build and of the tests.

cards.title: Wire the toggle into the shared layout and into the 5 screens
cards.body: Scope: the shared layout of the web app and the 5 screens, once both reviews are done. Steps: 1) place the toggle in the header and include the inline script in the head of the layout; 2) open each screen in both themes and fix what the tokens do not reach (images, shadows, the editor toolbar); 3) keep the existing components and class names where they already do the job; 4) check the result at 380 px and 1440 px, with the keyboard and with a pointer; 5) leave no error or warning in the console of the browser. Out of scope: the API, the content, a redesign of the screens that are not named. Acceptance criteria: no regression of the existing screens, keyboard use works end to end and the console stays empty. Proof: the diff, the output of the tests and before and after screenshots.

cards.title: Review the integration of the theme in the screens
cards.body: Scope: the diff of the card thint. Steps: 1) check that the script is included once, in the head, before any style sheet that paints; 2) open the 5 screens in both themes and compare with the light rendering of before; 3) run the build and the tests again and quote their real output; 4) look for a regression next to the change, not only in it; 5) number each finding and say how to reproduce it; 6) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked. Out of scope: rewriting the deliverable, widening the scope of the card reviewed. Acceptance criteria: a global verdict with numbered findings, each one reproducible, and nothing validated that was not checked. Proof: the review report with the real output of the build and of the tests.

cards.title: Audit the dark rendering of the 5 screens
cards.body: Scope: the real rendering of the 5 screens in the dark theme, on screenshots at 380 px and 1440 px. Steps: 1) judge hierarchy, legibility, focus rings, tags and the note cards against the light theme; 2) list each gap with its place, its measure and a severity; 3) say for each finding what would fix it, in one precise sentence; 4) compare with the reference of the project and name the gap; 5) end with one clear verdict; 6) judge the real rendering on screenshots, never the code; 7) give each finding a place, a measure and a severity (blocking, important, minor). Out of scope: any fix, any change of the content. Acceptance criteria: no finding rests on taste alone, each one points at a screenshot that shows it. Proof: the list of findings with the screenshot that proves each of them.

cards.title: Fix the visual and accessibility gaps that were reported
cards.body: Scope: the findings of the card daudit, and only them. Steps: 1) treat each finding in its order of severity and say which change answers it; 2) take the same screenshots again after the fixes; 3) respect the reduced-motion preference for anything that moves; 4) run the build and the tests before handing over; 5) keep the existing components and class names where they already do the job; 6) check the result at 380 px and 1440 px, with the keyboard and with a pointer. Out of scope: the server code, the copy of the interface, any new dependency. Acceptance criteria: the build passes, the rendering matches the reference on every screen named and nothing shifts while the page loads. Proof: the output of the build and screenshots of each state at both widths.

cards.title: Review the visual and accessibility fixes
cards.body: Scope: the diff of the card dfix against the findings of daudit. Steps: 1) check finding by finding that the fix is there and that it does what it says; 2) look for a regression of the light theme on the same screens; 3) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked; 4) measure it yourself instead of trusting the report of the card; 5) run the build and the tests again and quote their real output; 6) look for a regression next to the change, not only in it. Out of scope: fixing what you find yourself. Acceptance criteria: every criterion of the card reviewed is checked one by one and the verdict follows from the findings. Proof: the numbered findings and the commands that were run.

cards.title: Validate the final dark rendering after the fixes
cards.body: Scope: the screenshots taken again after the fixes, in both themes. Steps: 1) compare before and after for each finding of the audit; 2) give a verdict per screen, validated or to fix; 3) judge the real rendering on screenshots, never the code; 4) give each finding a place, a measure and a severity (blocking, important, minor); 5) say for each finding what would fix it, in one precise sentence; 6) compare with the reference of the project and name the gap. Out of scope: changing the code or the mock-up yourself, writing copy. Acceptance criteria: every finding is located, measured and comes with a precise recommendation, and the verdict is unambiguous. Proof: a report with the annotated screenshots.

cards.title: Test dark mode on the 5 screens of the app
cards.body: Scope: the 5 screens in a real browser, with the keyboard and with a pointer. Steps: 1) run the journeys write a note, search, change a setting and share a notebook in each theme; 2) write the missing non-regression tests of the toggle and of the stored choice; 3) try the edge cases: empty content, a very long title, a slow network, a second tab; 4) give each bug its steps, what was expected and what happened; 5) check the keyboard, both themes and three screen widths; 6) keep the tests that were written in the suite of the project. Out of scope: changing the code under test. Acceptance criteria: no journey is left untested and no bug is reported without its steps. Proof: the list of journeys with their result and the tests added.

cards.title: Review the tests and the non-regression report
cards.body: Scope: the tests and the report of the card qatest. Steps: 1) run the tests yourself and check that they fail when the toggle is removed; 2) read each bug of the report and reproduce two of them; 3) look for a regression next to the change, not only in it; 4) number each finding and say how to reproduce it; 5) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked. Out of scope: rewriting the deliverable, widening the scope of the card reviewed. Acceptance criteria: a global verdict with numbered findings, each one reproducible, and nothing validated that was not checked. Proof: the review report with the real output of the build and of the tests.

cards.title: Fix the dark mode bugs found by QA
cards.body: Scope: the bugs of the report of qatest, confirmed by the review. Steps: 1) reproduce each bug with its steps before touching the code; 2) fix it, then add or extend the test that would have caught it; 3) respect the reduced-motion preference for anything that moves; 4) run the build and the tests before handing over; 5) keep the existing components and class names where they already do the job. Out of scope: the API, the content, a redesign of the screens that are not named. Acceptance criteria: no regression of the existing screens, keyboard use works end to end and the console stays empty. Proof: the diff, the output of the tests and before and after screenshots.

cards.title: Review the fixes that came out of the tests
cards.body: Scope: the diff of the card fixqa. Steps: 1) check bug by bug that the steps of the report no longer reproduce it; 2) run the whole test suite and the build; 3) end with a verdict: validated, changes requested or blocked; 4) measure it yourself instead of trusting the report of the card; 5) run the build and the tests again and quote their real output. Out of scope: rewriting the deliverable, widening the scope of the card reviewed. Acceptance criteria: a global verdict with numbered findings, each one reproducible, and nothing validated that was not checked. Proof: the review report with the real output of the build and of the tests.

cards.title: Validate the final non-regression of dark mode
cards.body: Scope: the final state of the branch, in both themes. Steps: 1) run the journeys of qatest again on the 5 screens; 2) confirm that every bug of the report is closed and that the light theme is what it was; 3) use the real application in a real browser, as a user would; 4) try the edge cases: empty content, a very long title, a slow network, a second tab; 5) give each bug its steps, what was expected and what happened; 6) check the keyboard, both themes and three screen widths; 7) keep the tests that were written in the suite of the project. Out of scope: changing the code under test. Acceptance criteria: no journey is left untested and no bug is reported without its steps. Proof: the list of journeys with their result and the tests added.
